english: Along the wall you find a row of booths.
Any textiles are obviously ruined. But the wood itself stands. Interesting.
Your companion squats down and checks under the tables.
Yep. It's fucked down here too.
Where should I look first?
Happy to help.
The goblin glances to the other booths.
I'll look around, I guess.
Wherever evil is found.
Not helpful.
The left booth doesn't seem interesting.
Snell checks the right one.
Check the central booth.
The center. Your stomach buzzes with the possibility.
Magic is near. It contorts your innards.
Strange. Your body reacts in a way your senses do not follow.
The militia hosed the whole place down, Snell says while lifting a coal-like wood piece.
Especially here in the front. It's all sludge. Going to be hard finding any signs of... anything.
I'll just continue looking at this central booth, I guess.
Wouldn't that be neat, he says and drops the piece.
Yell if you find something.
Negative? He waggles the wood piece in your direction. "Realistic."
You focus on this particular booth. Or what used to be one.
The textiles once draped over the seating have been turned to ash and charred along with the expensive wood.
Along with the water damage, the elemental forces here are intense.
The stone tables remain standing for now, scorched like the dwarven architecture.
Yeah, no. I'm not finding anything here. I'll check the other booth.
He lifts his head and sniffs. "Keep looking for now. But let's not waste too much time here."
He's ordering you around. He can't do that.
The goblin is simply making conversation. Don't read into it.
The row of booths are still there. Still burnt to a crisp.
(Focus on the charred remains of the table.)
Look over the debris. Carefully.
E-Let's stop investigating this booth.
Glancing over the scorched wood you find it simply burned like everything else. Barely existing.
But it is wood. Intact wood, relatively speaking.
The militia's attempt to stop the fire splashed everything with water as well. So all the soot is just a sludge.
It is still quite strong- wedged along this stone bench.
R-(Put pressure on the broken piece.)
(Look at the ruined wood. Intensely.)
M-The table isn't that important.
You lean on it. The weight of your bulging muscles and overwhelming masculinity strains the thick timber. You can hear the wood fibers twitching...
You lean on it. You strain. It takes some effort, but soon you can hear the wood fibers twitching...
It snaps. You hold the piece of wood in your hands.
Your companion gives you a confounded look.
What, it wasn't ruined enough for you?
Great. Tea shop debris.
He shrugs. "Not like I'm gonna stop you."
Looking at the piece of wood, it's been infused with fiery energies.
Looking at the wood in your hand, you see that it is thick.
And sturdy.
Looking inside the burnt wood, you see a sliver of alive Brachen.
The thickness of the survived and burnt wood suggests a certain level of heat and firepower.
If this was caused by a Fireball spell... a regular 3rd level wouldn't do this kind of damage to Brachen.
Interesting.
Yep. That's a table.
If you don't have anything to add, don't say anything at all.
Come on... It's hard being quiet for this long. Go talk to someone!
You might as well check how sturdy it is, post-explosion.
Are you sure?
It is. Keep it in mind.
Lifting some of the wreckage, you spend ten minutes searching around the crevice behind the booth.
Until something catches your eye.
Something not burnt.
You reach out and grab it.
It's a tiny metal leaf. It fits in the palm of your gloved hand.
As you wipe off the soot you find it in a... strange condition. Its intricate design shows both value and style. But...
You feel a tingle down your arm. Esoterical.
You feel a tingle down your arm.
The tiny leaf fits in the palm of your gloved hand.
A magic item?
The brooch is half-melted.
A magic item does not get destroyed like this. Not by anything but the most powerful of magic.
It simply does not happen.
That's... a clue. Probably.
If this is magic, then it should not be easily destroyed.
A dainty elvish symbol. Representing their degeneracy and decadence.
This is a brooch designed by Illym hands. Their religious leaders and nobility carry these.
You glance over to your companion. He hasn't spotted your find yet.
(Just pocket it.)
He jumps, then gives you an angry glare.
Not so loud. Damn it.
Oh?
You put it away.
The goblin scoots on over to you and looks at the tiny pin in your hand.
Strange. Interesting.
It... kind of survived the fire?
Bring it with. Show it to the Old Lady.
Sure.
Why would she care?
I don't think it's relevant.
Obviously she'd care.
Alright. Sure.
But it's not relevant.
You don't think a clearly magical piece of jewelry inside of this exploded tea shop would be a relevant clue?
Well, when you put it like that...
No.
Yeah.
Right.
He looks around.
Let's focus somewhere else in here.
You spend ten minutes searching the ruined booths.
You spot nothing out of the ordinary.
Ordinary being soot, scorched wood, and general ruinousness.
Ruinousness is not a word.
It is not? Apologies.
Nothing, your companion says with a sigh. "Can't find nothing."
Let's look somewhere else.
